title: Design Brief
description: Structured outcome of the create-design-system Design Interview. It is the visual contract for a generated design-system package. `pnpm ds:create --brief <path>` reads this file, normalizes only the fields it uses, preserves unknown extra fields, and writes a copy to the generated package as design-brief.json; the generator does not perform full schema validation. Unknown extra fields are allowed so the interview can record decisions this schema does not yet enumerate. The written design-brief.json ships in the package tarball: keep only sanitized product and visual intent, with no secrets, customer-sensitive data, private reference URLs, personal details, or interview transcripts.

project.description: Human-facing name of the product or project the design system serves. The generator uses it as the package display name when --name is omitted and writes it into README.md and AGENTS.md.

product.description: One-sentence description of what the product is.
examples: Developer productivity application for inspecting CI pipelines

audience.description: Primary users of the product and the context in which they use it.
examples: Professional developers working long sessions on desktop

interfaceType.description: The kind of interface being designed.

dataDensity.description: How information-dense the interface is expected to be. Drives spacing, control height, and typography scale decisions.

direction.description: Short adjectives describing the intended feel, such as compact, technical, dark-first, restrained, low visual noise. The generator joins these into the package visual direction.

references.description: Existing products or interfaces the user likes visually, used as shared vocabulary for the visual direction.

foundations.description: Concrete visual foundation decisions for the system. Extra fields are allowed so the interview can record decisions this schema does not yet enumerate.

accentDirection.description: Intended accent hue and how much it is used.

contrast.description: How much contrast surfaces and text should carry.

typographyCharacter.description: Personality and hierarchy of the type system.
examples: neutral grotesk with strong hierarchy and dense body text

dominantRadius.description: Typical corner radius of controls and surfaces.

surfaceModel.description: How surfaces stack and separate from each other.

examples: minimal borders, rely on surface separation

motionIntensity.description: How much motion the system should use.

components.description: Legacy-compatible mixed notes about components and scenarios. Keep existing briefs valid; new briefs should classify reusable capability requests and product compositions in the optional fields below instead of treating every note as a component request.

requestedCapabilities.description: Optional requests for reusable capabilities, especially optional core contracts. Requests are intent only: the package descriptor and generated public manifest define actual available capabilities.

productCompositions.description: Optional whole-product page, form, workflow, and domain-specific composition scenarios to guide the visual system. These do not become component contracts merely by appearing here.
examples: Responsive project overview with activity table

responsiveRequirements.description: Optional concrete behavior expected across target viewport sizes, such as navigation changes, content reflow, and dense-table treatment.
examples: At narrow widths, stack filters above results
Keep primary actions reachable without horizontal scrolling

typographyRequirements.description: Optional hierarchy and legibility requirements for headings, body copy, labels, metadata, and dense data. Older briefs may omit this; the interview can derive it from foundations.typographyCharacter.

stateScenarios.description: Optional complete-page or form loading, error, empty, success, and validation scenarios to design and review.

referenceNotes.description: Optional notes about specific references, naming the traits to take and the traits not to copy, for example "Linear - take: compact density and restrained accent; avoid: copying its exact palette". Do not repeat a value already listed in references; the two fields together record the reference name and what it means.
examples: Linear - take: compact density and restrained accent; avoid: copying its exact palette
Raycast - take: command-palette hierarchy; avoid: dark-only assumption

decisionNotes.description: Optional significant decisions and choices from the interview. Record only decisions that matter to the visual system, not every microdecision, and do not repeat values another field already owns: a note carries the decision and its rationale. Status meanings: confirmed = the user provided or approved the decision; delegated = the user explicitly let the agent decide; proposed = the agent proposed it and the user has not decided yet. A generator-ready brief contains no material proposed decision.

examples.note: The user chose a cool blue accent used only for primary actions.
The user delegated the foundations; the agent chose restrained contrast and minimal elevation to fit the confirmed direction.

openQuestions.description: Optional open questions from the interview. In a draft brief, a pending material question is a reason the brief is not generator-ready. In an approved generator-ready brief, only nonblocking follow-ups that do not change approved decisions may remain.
examples: Illustration style for a future marketing surface, outside the approved console scope

avoid.description: Visual decisions that must be avoided. The generator joins these into the package avoid list in README.md and AGENTS.md.

decisionNote.description: One significant design decision. `status` distinguishes an answer the user gave or approved (confirmed), explicit permission for the agent to decide (delegated), and a choice still awaiting the user (proposed).

topic.description: Short name of the decision area, for example "accent color" or "density".

status.description: confirmed = the user provided or approved the decision; delegated = the user explicitly let the agent decide; proposed = the agent proposed it and the user has not decided yet. A generator-ready brief must contain no material proposed decision.

note.description: The decision and its reason, in one sentence. Do not repeat a value owned by another field; record the choice and rationale instead.
